claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch, and that certification can be defended without a material-weakness disclosure, based on aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance on documentation and ongoing monitoring.
specific_concerns: The policy text says a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and the actor summary says the below-target Spanish-language billing support segment is named in three international pilot commitments.
The actor summary states legal review on disclosure remains open, which the policy text identifies as a reason product labels do not resolve materiality.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness but do not by themselves resolve whether a material weakness disclosure is required.
Public model-card and risk-management guidance supports documentation and monitoring in general, but does not independently satisfy the case-specific materiality predicate.
unsupported_claims: That certification without a material-weakness disclosure is adequately supported by the admissible record.
That the product note describing the segment as non-core is sufficient to defeat materiality.
Any implicit claim that public governance guidance can substitute for a resolved legal or policy determination on disclosure.
evidence_requests: The actual text or determination from the pending legal review on whether the Spanish-language billing support gap must be disclosed.
The underlying contractual or pilot-commitment documents showing whether the affected segment is a named committed use case.
The exact internal threshold, measurement methodology, and segment-level results used to determine the 2.1-point miss.
Any formal waiver, approval, or policy exception authorizing certification despite an unresolved potentially material gap.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for certification and any disclosure obligations.
Treat unresolved materiality predicates as outcome-determinative where policy text makes them mandatory.
Do not let aggregate launch readiness substitute for evidence that a named affected segment is non-material or properly disclosed.
General public AI governance guidance can support process quality, but not replace case-specific proof on contractual-segment materiality.
